hypothesis: The serial r-k-c variant was valid at a 0.076396257 s mean, and adding an explicit c-dimension SIMD directive without threads measured 0.073052032 s; row-parallel r-k-c measured 0.009476691 s. This experiment tests whether combining static row parallelism, capped by the caller's thread count, with contiguous c-dimension SIMD improves on row parallelism alone. Each output element retains ascending-k accumulation and C is cleared on every call. The combined effect remains unmeasured.
notes: Earlier measurements provide context, not a result for this candidate: the baseline mean was 6.405855497 s; serial r-k-c was 0.076396257 s; serial r-k-c with SIMD was 0.073052032 s; row-parallel r-k-c was 0.009476691 s. This version combines row parallelism and SIMD, so it does not isolate either change against the baseline. No new correctness or timing tests were run here; the controller should check all official sizes and repeated native n=1024 timings. No integration sources were supplied.
transformations: Replace fixed-size dispatch with runtime dimensions so the kernel handles valid sizes without specializing to the official benchmark sizes.
Clear the complete output before accumulating with an r-k-c traversal, preserving ascending-k accumulation for each output element.
Parallelize independent output rows with static scheduling and at most min(n, threads) workers; use a serial path when the available worker count is at most one.
Apply OpenMP SIMD to the innermost contiguous c traversal as the single follow-up interaction test.
